scoring_note: Weights: freshness 10, growth 15, reach 15, qualified-follower potential 15, regional business relevance 15, audience psychology 10, commercial utility 10, originality 5, verifiability 5. growth, reach, follower potential, relevance, psychology, utility and originality are subjective estimates; nothing here is claimed as a verified trend.

candidates.title: Uniqlo scraps its ¥100 sock price rise in Japan 11 days after announcing it; jacket and trouser rises go ahead
candidates.claim: 16 Oct: Uniqlo announced price revisions from 10 Nov, incl. 50-colour socks ¥290->¥390 and ending 4-for-¥990 / 3-for-¥990 bundles (4 colour socks ¥990->¥1,560, ~+58%). 27 Oct: notice updated, sock changes cancelled, apology for changing so soon; Kando Jacket ¥6,990->¥7,990 and Kando Pants ¥3,990->¥4,990 still rise on 10 Nov. Average selling price was to rise ~4%.
candidates.verification: verified: AdverTimes (28 Oct), FASHIONSNAP (27 Oct), AFP via Arab News Japan (29 Oct), Bloomberg via The Star (29 Oct), Herald Business, Seoul Economic Daily (30 Oct). Fast Retailing spokesperson: 'As socks are an essential everyday item, in Japan we reconsidered our planned price revision.' Social outcry on X reported (anonymous posts, no numbers). Japan Times and FashionNetwork fetches failed.
candidates.notes: Strongest tension in the set: the small rise on the everyday item was reversed, the bigger rises on considered items stayed. Inflation-era pricing is acutely relevant to Persian-speaking and regional business owners.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: Verified across AdverTimes, FASHIONSNAP, AFP, Bloomberg (via The Star), Herald Business, SEDaily: socks ¥290->¥390 and bundle removal announced 16 Oct, cancelled 27 Oct (11 days), apology; jacket ¥6,990->¥7,990 and pants ¥3,990->¥4,990 proceed 10 Nov. NOT verified: that nobody complained about the jacket rise (do not say so; say 'the jacket rise stayed'); size of the outcry (anonymous X posts only); Uniqlo's internal reasoning beyond 'socks are an essential everyday item'. The 'socks are Uniqlo's milk and eggs' reading is OUR interpretation via the KVI concept (McKinsey as cited by Food Trade News) — present as a reading. Japan CPI figures conflict across sources (2.1% vs 3.2%): do not use. Saizeriya customer support: unverified, do not claim.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Everyone owns cheap socks; ¥100 is small and universal; the paradox (small rise punished, big rise tolerated) creates instant curiosity. Mechanism: customers don't remember most prices, they remember a few reference prices that stand for 'is this place fair?'; touching those feels like breaking a promise, while considered purchases are compared on quality. Strong for inflation-weary Persian audience and for café/shop owners raising prices now.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Pricing communication and brand promise: squarely in scope. Practical takeaway for owners: find your 'socks' (the item people use to judge you), protect or move it last; raise where value is visible; say it plainly. Not a lecture on economics; no politics; avoid naming any country's inflation level.

gates.brand_fit: pass: C1+C2 merged; C5 fails repetition (10-30), C8 fails repetition (10-31) and verification, C10 fails repetition (11-01), C11 weak business fit, C7/C12 stale.
gates.story_gate: winner: C1+C2 — tension '¥1,000 more on a jacket stayed; ¥100 more on socks didn't last 11 days'; concrete image: a single pair of plain socks next to a jacket on a hanger, price tags swapping. Runner-up C3 (how you say a price rise) kept as caption aside.

decision.why: Highest total (C1 94); breaking spark with an evergreen body (key value items: customers judge your prices by a few prices); universal for Persian and international audiences; most concrete everyday image; no overlap with last 7 days.
